page: Microsoft Azure E8d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Advanced instruction set extensions are available, including AVX-512, AVX512 VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware allocation includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The E8d_v5 variant integrates 322 GB of local SSD temporary storage directly attached to the host, distinguishing it from non-disk variants in the EDv5 family. Network architecture provisions zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and the instance operates without dedicated GPU acceleration hardware.

Benchmark measurements position the E8d_v5 predominantly in the middle 50% across compute, memory, and application-level workloads. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 11353.2, a Geekbench 6 multi-core score of 5872.0, and a single-core score of 1572.0. Memory throughput yields 56.69 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 40.14 GB/sec in write operations. Key-value operations reflect solid caching capability with Redis SET throughput reaching 7.75 million operations per second, alongside PassMark database operation scores of 4029.97 and static web throughput of 10.97 GB/sec.

Performance constraints appear under heavy parallel decompression and transformer workloads. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 7B parameter LLM inference throughput fall into the lower quartile, reflecting compute limitations relative to the memory footprint. The 8:1 memory-to-core configuration delivers balanced operational economics for enterprise relational databases, in-memory caches, search indexes, and stateful analytical applications requiring moderate compute density paired with fast local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure E8d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, running on a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. Based on the x86_64 architecture with 4 physical cores and hyper-threading, the instance features hardware support for AVX-512, AES-NI, and SHA extensions alongside 48 MB of L3 cache. It includes 322 GB of local SSD storage and operates without GPU acceleration. Across synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates consistent mid-tier performance, producing a PassMark CPU score of 11353.2, 5872.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 7.75 million Redis SET operations per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 7B LLM inference fall into lower quartiles due to core count constraints relative to memory size. The instance provides effective resource density for memory-bound workloads such as in-memory caches, relational database systems, and data processing pipelines needing fast local scratch disks.
